inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted: 2,363.0m ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (AR note 27) + 1,719.4m shares issuable under the 2010 convertible notes held by SHKP/Sunco (HK$0.10 conversion price, already included in the company's own basic and diluted EPS denominator of 4,083.6m) + ~16m exercisable share options (note 29); rounded to 4,100m. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; no buybacks (none in FY2025 or FY2026).
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank borrowings HK$10,997.966m (994.0 current + 10,003.966 non-current, note 25, effective rate 3.40%) + SHKP shareholder's loans HK$5,000m (note 26, floating rate, treated as debt) = HK$15,997.966m; less cash HK$426.564m. Lease liabilities HK$169.1m EXCLUDED under lease treatment (B). Undrawn facilities ~HK$3,550m at 30 June 2026.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf follows the house formula (reported FCF 1,902.1 less SBC 19.4; interest income not stripped because the company is net-debt, not net-cash). It is NOT a clean base: FY2026 OCF includes a +HK$477.1m increase in contract liabilities (an upfront lump-sum prepayment from a hyperscale customer at MEGA IDC Phase One, note 22; HK$443.0m of it non-current). Stripping that gives ~HK$1,405.6m of underlying owner FCF, which is what the component build's year-1 should be compared against. The projections start from revenue and components, so the one-off does not propagate.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income HK$7.9m left in the flows: net debt is HK$15.6bn, so there is no cash pile being double-counted.
inputs.sbc_source: 1686.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt (FY2026 annual report, year ended 30 June 2026) cash flow statement line 'Equity-settled share-based payments' HK$19,433k; no net-share-settlement taxes (options are exercised for cash).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z (HKEX regular close, Yahoo Finance chart API)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in HKD (USD-pegged). Risk-free: 10-year HK Exchange Fund Note ~3.6%. Cost of equity ~9.5% (beta ~0.95 for a single-market data-centre operator, ERP 6.0%, plus a small premium for 100% Hong Kong concentration). Cost of debt: FY2026 effective bank rate 3.40% is a cyclical low on 100% floating-rate borrowings; normalised at ~5.0% pre-tax / ~4.2% post-tax (HK 16.5%). Weights at market: equity ~HK$20.7bn (4,100m x price) vs net debt HK$15.6bn = 57/43. 0.57 x 9.5% + 0.43 x 4.2% = 7.2%, rounded up to 7.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, AI-capex dependence and leverage are charged in the flows, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost: full lease payment (FY2026 principal HK$22.0m + lease interest HK$5.4m = HK$27.4m, 0.88% of revenue) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (HK$169.1m) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation on leased properties (HK$677.6m - HK$22.6m = HK$655.0m, 21.0% of revenue). Leasehold-land amortisation (HK$81.6m on owned sites) stays in D&A: it is HK land tenure on owned data centres, not an operating lease.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI HK$2.0m (0.03% of equity) ignored as immaterial; flows are effectively 100% attributable. Equity instruments at FVTOCI HK$4.5m also ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (FY2027-FY2036). Routing: SUNeVision is an internally managed operating company that owns and builds its own data centres (PP&E at cost, HK$23.8bn, no IAS 40 fair-value model, no external manager) so the REIT/AFFO row does not apply; the SKILL's 'infrastructure in a capex supercycle' note is why reported FCF is modelled explicitly through a capex path rather than read as a signal. NAV cross-check recorded as a memo in valuation_philosophy (independent valuer: operating data centres HK$51.5bn, implying equity HK$40.8bn / ~HK$9.95 per diluted share). KEY MODELLING FACT: management is building MEGA IDC Phases 2/3 as one integrated ~700,000 sq ft / ~130MW development targeted ready-for-service 2028 (GFA 2.3m -> ~3.0m sq ft, power 150MW -> 280MW). The capex path front-loads ~HK$7.9bn over FY2027-FY2029 (base), driving owner FCF to around zero or negative for two years, with the revenue step-up arriving FY2029-FY2031 as the new capacity leases up. Interest paid (FY2026 HK$548.7m; FY2025 HK$808.8m) is mostly capitalised and sits in financing activities, so capex (HK$774.4m) is ex-interest, consistent with an unlevered build. Cash tax (HK$81.6m vs HK$227.5m P&L charge) is depressed by capital allowances on the buildout and is ramped toward ~15% as capex normalises. SBC-light market: band is narrow but non-zero. Price is the HKEX regular close of 16 Oct 2026, not after-hours.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3-yr CAGR (11.5%) exceeds EPS 3-yr CAGR (8.0%) by >30% relative because the dividend payout was cut from ~93% of earnings (FY2023) to ~43% (FY2024-FY2026) to fund the buildout; retained earnings, not operating acceleration, drove the book-value step-up. Equity 5-yr (7.8%) agrees with EPS 5-yr (7.7%).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined: the SBC-adjusted owner-FCF series is negative in FY2021 (-570.4), FY2022 (-440.8), FY2023 (-490.6) and FY2024 (-1,398.3) because capex ran ahead of operating cash flow during the MEGA IDC Phase One and MEGA Gateway builds, turning positive only in FY2025 (670.2) and FY2026 (1,882.7, of which ~HK$477m is a one-off contract-liability inflow). Reported FCF CAGRs are equally undefined; structurally negative FCF here is the capex cycle, not distress (OCF grew 16.1% p.a. over 5 years, from 1,266.5 to 2,676.5). SBC is 0.6% of revenue and has grown slower than cash flow, so there is no hidden SBC-funded growth. The base near-term growth anchor (8%) is the equity/EPS 5-yr CAGR; the FY2029-FY2031 step-up is the modelled lease-up of the MEGA IDC Phase 2/3 capacity, not an extrapolation.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027-28 +8% = equity/EPS 5-yr CAGR plus Phase One occupancy rising from ~30% to ~70% on the signed hyperscale commitment and positive rental reversion on the two largest-customer renewals. FY2029-31 +18/+18/+12 = lease-up of the ~130MW Phase 2/3 capacity (RFS 2028) at wholesale hyperscale pricing of ~HK$15-20m per MW-year (below the ~HK$27m/MW the retail/MEGA-i-weighted installed base earns), reaching ~70% utilisation by FY2031; FY2031 revenue ~HK$5.7bn. Then fade to 3% as Hong Kong power and land gate further supply.
base.capex_rationale: Phase 2/3 integrated build (~700,000 sq ft, ~130MW) plus Phase One fit-out and HK$933m already contracted: ~HK$2.4bn FY2027, ~HK$3.1bn FY2028, ~HK$2.4bn FY2029 (total ~HK$7.9bn, roughly HK$55-60m per MW all-in excluding land, which is owned). Thereafter 17-18% of revenue: maintenance plus density/liquid-cooling retrofits on the installed base. Capex is ex capitalised interest (interest paid sits in financing).
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 EBITDA margin 73.8% (company basis, ex interest income). Dips to 72.5% in FY2029 as new wholesale capacity opens before it is fully leased and power pass-through dilutes the mix, then recovers to 74%. No expansion beyond the FY2026 level is assumed.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 cash tax HK$81.6m vs P&L HK$227.5m (16.5% statutory): capital allowances on the buildout defer tax. Held at 5-6% of EBIT while Phase 2/3 capex runs, then ramped to 15% by FY2035 (slightly below statutory for ongoing deferral on maintenance capex).
base.da_rationale: 21.0% of revenue ex-ROU in FY2026; rises to 22% as ~HK$8bn of new plant is commissioned FY2029-30, then eases back as revenue catches up.

bull.rationale: AI-inference demand proves durable: Phase One fills (two further hyperscale floors signed), Phase 2/3 is substantially pre-committed before RFS and leases to ~90% by FY2031 at scarcity pricing; MEGA-i interconnection and densification retrofits lift margins toward 76%. Upfront customer prepayments recur (wc_capture 10% of revenue growth). Same capex envelope, more revenue per MW. Terminal cap 20x reflects infrastructure-grade cash flows in a power-constrained market.

bear.rationale: The integrated Phase 2/3 build is committed and gets spent (same FY2027-29 capex in HK$ terms as base, since the percentages apply to lower revenue only modestly), but an AI-capex pause plus peers' new supply leaves it leasing up slowly at lower rents; Phase One stalls near 70%. Margins compress to 70% on under-utilised power and competitive pricing. Floating-rate debt on HK$16bn is not in the unlevered flows but caps the terminal multiple at 15x: a buyer of a 100%-Hong-Kong, 45%-geared asset in a softer market pays less. Cash tax normalises faster as capex slows.

scenario_narratives.base: SUNeVision's value turns on two axes: whether the ~130MW MEGA IDC Phase 2/3 build (RFS 2028) leases up at hyperscale wholesale rents, and what it costs to get there. Base assumes Phase One goes from ~30% to ~70%+ on the signed commitment, Phase 2/3 reaches ~70% utilisation by FY2031 at ~HK$15-20m/MW-year, revenue reaches ~HK$5.7bn by FY2031 (FY2026: HK$3.1bn), EBITDA margin holds at 73-74%, and ~HK$7.9bn of capex over FY2027-29 pushes owner FCF to around zero for two years before it rebuilds to ~HK$2.5-3bn/yr. The FY2026 HK$477m contract-liability inflow is treated as a one-off. Net debt of HK$15.6bn (including HK$5bn SHKP loans) is deducted once at the end; the hurdle on an asset that is ~70% terminal value is steep.
scenario_narratives.bull: Hong Kong's power and land constraints bind harder on peers than on SUNeVision: Phase One fills with the two additional hyperscale floors, Phase 2/3 is pre-committed before RFS and fills to ~90% by FY2031 at scarcity pricing, MEGA-i's ~15,000 cross-connects and densification retrofits lift margins toward 76%, and upfront prepayments recur. Revenue ~HK$6.6bn by FY2031, ~HK$8.3bn by FY2036; terminal cap 20x for infrastructure-grade cash flows.
scenario_narratives.bear: A hyperscaler AI-capex pause coincides with the integrated Phase 2/3 build landing in 2028 alongside peer supply; the capex is spent but utilisation lags, Hong Kong keeps losing subsea-cable share to Singapore, rents soften and margins fall to 70%. Revenue only reaches ~HK$4.4bn by FY2031. The unlevered flows survive but a 15x terminal cap on a 45%-geared single-market asset leaves equity worth a fraction of the base case: the leverage is what makes the bear case bite.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 default to 25/50/25. Bear raised to 25% because the equity sits behind HK$16bn of 100%-floating-rate debt (gearing 38% on appraised values including SHKP loans), the growth thesis depends on one city's power grid and on the global AI capex cycle, and the Phase 2/3 build is a single HK$8bn-class execution bet; the SHKP backing mitigates refinancing but not utilisation risk. Bull cut to 25% because it needs AI demand, pre-commitment timing and scarcity pricing all to hold simultaneously through 2031.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Unlevered owner-FCF DCF on a 10-year explicit horizon because the FY2027-29 capex supercycle makes any shorter horizon capitalise either a negative FCF year or an immature margin. Value is dominated by the terminal (~70% of EV) and by the capacity step-up that the new build enables; the HK$15.6bn net debt is deducted once. Memo NAV cross-check: the independent valuer's HK$51.5bn fair value for the operating data centres implies equity of HK$40.8bn, or ~HK$9.95 per diluted share, against the DCF base; the market price is ~50% of that appraised NAV. The gap between the DCF base and the appraisal is largely the appraiser's lower discount rate on a stabilised asset versus this model's 7.5% WACC on a business still spending ~HK$8bn of growth capex, and is reported, not used.
key_risks_to_valuation: Lease-up timing and pricing of the ~130MW MEGA IDC Phase 2/3 capacity (RFS 2028): a two-year slip or wholesale rents of HK$12m/MW instead of HK$15-20m takes the base toward the bear case
Capex overrun on the integrated build: each HK$1bn of extra capex is ~HK$0.22/share before any revenue offset
Floating-rate HK$16bn debt: not in the unlevered flows, but a HIBOR spike raises the effective cost of capital and the refinancing dependence on SHKP
Terminal value is ~70% of EV; the 18x cap binds in base (Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would be 20.5x), so the valuation is sensitive to the exit multiple a buyer pays for a Hong Kong-only asset
Cash tax ramp: if capital allowances keep cash tax near 5% indefinitely the base is understated; if they exhaust faster, overstated
Single-market concentration (100% Hong Kong) and geopolitical/cross-border data-flow risk for Chinese and US hyperscaler tenants
